questions.question: Which cabinet minister of Inda in June 2025 held bilateral talks with Dong Jun of China at the conclave of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) in the Chinese port city of Qingdao, with a focus on maintaining peace and tranquillity along the Line of Actual Control (LAC)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Raj Nath Singh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Raj Nath Singh**, the Defence Minister of India, held bilateral talks with **Dong Jun**, a senior Chinese official, during the **Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) conclave** in **June 2025**.
 
• The discussions took place in the **Chinese port city of Qingdao**, which has previously hosted high-profile international summits.
 
• The talks primarily focused on maintaining **peace and tranquillity along the Line of Actual Control (LAC)**, which is the de facto border between India and China.
 
• The meeting aimed to address ongoing border tensions and reinforce agreements to avoid escalations in sensitive areas, particularly in regions like **Eastern Ladakh**.
 
• Raj Nath Singh also emphasized the importance of resolving disputes through **diplomatic and peaceful means**, aligning with India's consistent approach to international relations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO):**

 
 
• The SCO is a regional intergovernmental organization established in **2001**, with a primary focus on political, economic, and security cooperation.
 
• Its founding members include China, Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, and Uzbekistan. India and Pakistan joined as full members in **2017**.
 
• The organization provides a platform for member states to collaborate on issues like counter-terrorism, border security, and economic development.
 
 
 
• **Line of Actual Control (LAC):**
 
 
• The LAC is a 3,488 km long boundary between **India and China**, separating Indian-controlled territory from Chinese-controlled territory.
 
• It is divided into three sectors: the **Western Sector** (Ladakh), the **Middle Sector** (Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand), and the **Eastern Sector** (Sikkim and Arunachal Pradesh).
 
• Frequent tensions arise along the LAC, requiring diplomatic and military engagement to maintain stability.
 
 
 
• **India-China Border Relations:**
 
 
• The two nations have a history of border disputes, with significant conflicts like the **1962 Sino-Indian War** and recent standoffs like the **Galwan Valley clash in 2020**.
 
• To manage disputes, both countries have signed agreements such as the **1993 Border Peace and Tranquillity Agreement** and the **1996 Confidence-Building Measures Agreement**.
 
• Despite agreements, incidents of transgressions and military build-ups continue to strain relations.
 
 
 
• **Raj Nath Singh:**
 
 
• He is a senior leader of the **Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)** and has served as the **Defence Minister of India** since **2019**.
 
• Under his leadership, India has strengthened its defence capabilities and emphasized self-reliance through the **Atmanirbhar Bharat** initiative in the defence sector.
 
• He has played a key role in addressing border security challenges and modernizing the armed forces.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Qingdao:**

 
 
• A major port city in **Shandong Province, China**, known for hosting international events like the **SCO Summit** in 2018.
 
• It is strategically significant due to its location and infrastructure, making it a preferred venue for diplomatic engagements.
 
 
 
• **Significance of India-China Talks:**
 
 
• Such bilateral meetings are crucial for reducing border tensions and fostering cooperation in other areas like trade and regional security.
 
• They also reflect India's commitment to peaceful conflict resolution and adherence to international norms.
 
 
 
• **India’s Defence Diplomacy:**
 
 
• India has been actively engaging with international partners through platforms like the **Quad, SCO, and BRICS** to strengthen its strategic partnerships.
 
• The Defence Minister's participation in global forums underscores India's increasing role in shaping regional and global security dynamics.

questions.question: Who announced the launch of India’s first homegrown semiconductor chip in May 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajeev Chandrasekhar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Rajeev Chandrasekhar**, who is the **Minister of State for Electronics and Information Technology** in India, announced the launch of **India’s first homegrown semiconductor chip** in **May 2025**.
 
• The announcement marked a significant milestone for India’s ambition to become a global hub for **semiconductor manufacturing** and reduce dependence on imports.
 
• This initiative is part of the broader **Semicon India Programme**, launched by the government to develop a robust semiconductor ecosystem in the country with a **financial outlay of Rs. 76,000 crore**.
 
• The homegrown semiconductor chip is expected to bolster India's position in the global electronics supply chain, which has been disrupted due to geopolitical tensions and the pandemic.
 
• Semiconductors are the backbone of modern electronics, including **smartphones, laptops, automobiles, and defense equipment**. This development is aligned with the government’s mission of **Aatmanirbhar Bharat (Self-Reliant India)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Semicon India Programme:**

 
 
• Launched by the **Government of India** in **December 2021**, the programme aims to establish India as a global hub for semiconductor design, manufacturing, and technology development.
 
• It includes initiatives to attract investments from global semiconductor companies and foster **research and development** in this field.
 
• The programme is expected to create job opportunities and enhance India's capabilities in critical technologies.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Semiconductors:**
 
 
• Semiconductors are essential components in electronic devices such as **microprocessors, sensors, and memory chips**.
 
• They enable the functioning of various sectors, including **telecommunications, healthcare, automotive, and defense**.
 
• India has been heavily dependent on imports for its semiconductor needs, making the development of indigenous chips a strategic move.
 
 
 
• **Rajeev Chandrasekhar’s Role:**
 
 
• Rajeev Chandrasekhar is a prominent Indian politician and entrepreneur with expertise in technology and innovation.
 
• He has been actively involved in shaping India’s digital economy and promoting initiatives like **Digital India** and **Make in India**.
 
• As the Minister of State for Electronics and IT, he has played a crucial role in the formulation and execution of policies aimed at enhancing India’s technological capabilities.
 
 
 
• **Global Semiconductor Market:**
 
 
• The global semiconductor market was valued at approximately **USD 555.9 billion** in 2021 and is expected to grow significantly in the coming years.
 
• The demand for semiconductors has been driven by advancements in **5G technology, artificial intelligence, and IoT (Internet of Things)**.
 
• India’s entry into semiconductor manufacturing is expected to increase its competitiveness in the global market and reduce reliance on imports from countries like **China and Taiwan**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Challenges in Semiconductor Manufacturing:**

 
 
• Setting up a semiconductor fabrication unit is capital-intensive, requiring investments ranging from **USD 3 billion to USD 15 billion**.
 
• The process involves complex technological requirements, including **cleanrooms, equipment, and skilled professionals**.
 
• India faces challenges in terms of infrastructure, supply chain development, and the availability of raw materials like silicon wafers.
 
 
 
• **Global Supply Chain Issues:**
 
 
• The semiconductor industry has faced disruptions due to the **COVID-19 pandemic** and geopolitical tensions, leading to a global chip shortage.
 
• India’s initiative to develop homegrown chips is a step towards reducing dependency on global supply chains and ensuring self-reliance.
 
 
 
• **Future Prospects:**
 
 
• The success of India’s semiconductor initiative will depend on its ability to attract investments, develop skilled manpower, and create a conducive business environment.
 
• Collaborations with global technology leaders and academic institutions will be crucial for building a robust semiconductor ecosystem.
 
• India’s efforts in this sector are expected to contribute significantly to its **GDP growth** and technological advancements.

questions.question: Which organ under MHA launched the e‑Zero FIR system for cyber‑fraud cases?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C)**, which operates under the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA), launched the **e-Zero FIR system** to help tackle cyber fraud cases.
 
• This initiative aims to allow victims of **cybercrime** to file a First Information Report (FIR) online, even if the crime occurs outside their jurisdiction.
 
• The **e-Zero FIR system** is part of the government’s broader effort to address the growing issue of **cybercrimes** and ensure that victims receive timely assistance in reporting and resolving such cases.
 
• The I4C was established in **2018** and became fully operational in **2020** to combat cybercrime and oversee the implementation of related policies nationwide.
 
• This platform is integrated with the **National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal**, which serves as a centralized platform to file complaints related to various cybercrimes, including financial fraud, identity theft, and online harassment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C):**

 
 
• The I4C was established to handle **cybercrime prevention, investigation, and capacity building** in India.
 
• It acts as a nodal agency to coordinate efforts among various states and union territories to combat cybercrime.
 
• The I4C comprises **seven components**, including a National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal, a research and innovation center, and a training ecosystem to enhance cybercrime investigation skills.
 
• Its major goal is to create a safe and secure cyberspace in India.
 
 
 
• **National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal:**
 
 
• The portal was launched under the I4C initiative to allow citizens to **report cybercrimes online**.
 
• It primarily focuses on crimes against women and children, such as **online harassment, child pornography, and cyberstalking**.
 
• The platform also handles cases related to **financial fraud**, including UPI or debit/credit card frauds.
 
• The portal has been designed to be **user-friendly** and accessible to people from all regions of India.
 
 
 
• **Cybercrime in India:**
 
 
• India has witnessed a significant rise in cybercrimes due to the increasing penetration of **digital platforms** and online financial transactions.
 
• According to the **National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB)**, cybercrime cases in India have been steadily increasing, with financial frauds being the most common.
 
• The government has introduced several measures, including the establishment of **cyber forensic laboratories** and the promotion of awareness campaigns to educate citizens about cyber safety.
 
 
 
• **Other Organizations under MHA:**
 
 
• The **Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI)** investigates high-profile crimes, including corruption and economic offenses, but does not primarily handle cybercrimes.
 
• The **Cyber Appellate Tribunal**, established under the IT Act 2000, handles appeals related to cyber law cases but does not oversee the implementation of cybercrime prevention systems.
 
• The **State Police** departments handle cybercrime cases at the local level but rely on centralized platforms like I4C for advanced tools and coordination.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **e-Zero FIR system** ensures that victims of cybercrime can file FIRs without jurisdictional barriers, making it easier for law enforcement to investigate cases.
 
• The I4C’s efforts align with the government’s **Digital India initiative**, which aims to enhance digital security and promote the safe use of technology.
 
• Citizens are encouraged to report cybercrimes promptly to prevent further damage and assist law enforcement in tracking offenders.
 
• The government has also introduced awareness programs on cyber hygiene to educate people about secure online practices.

questions.question: Which of the following ministries launched the State Health Regulatory Excellence Index (SHRESTH), a first-of-its-kind national initiative to benchmark and strengthen state drug regulatory systems through a transparent, data-driven framework in August 2025?

options.text: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ministry of Health and Family Welfare**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **State Health Regulatory Excellence Index (SHRESTH)** was launched by the **Ministry of Health and Family Welfare** in **August 2025**.
 
• It is a **first-of-its-kind national initiative** aiming to **benchmark and strengthen state drug regulatory systems** through a **transparent and data-driven framework**.
 
• The primary goal of SHRESTH is to enhance the **efficiency, transparency, and accountability** of drug regulatory systems across different states.
 
• This initiative is expected to ensure that **quality medicines** are accessible to citizens by improving the regulation and monitoring of pharmaceutical products.
 
• The **Ministry of Health and Family Welfare** plays a pivotal role in ensuring the implementation of the framework, addressing gaps in the existing drug regulatory systems.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **State Health Regulatory Excellence Index (SHRESTH):**

 
 
• This initiative aims to create a **robust mechanism** for state drug regulators to identify their strengths and weaknesses.
 
• It provides a **standardized evaluation system** and promotes a **uniform regulatory framework** for pharmaceuticals across India.
 
• Data and analytics play a significant role in ensuring **evidence-based decision-making** for policymakers and regulators.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Health and Family Welfare:**
 
 
• This ministry is responsible for the implementation of **health-related schemes** and policies in India.
 
• It oversees the regulation of **pharmaceuticals, medical devices, and healthcare services** in the country.
 
• Some of its other key initiatives include **Ayushman Bharat**, the **National Health Mission**, and the **National Digital Health Mission**.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Drug Regulatory Systems:**
 
 
• **Drug regulation** ensures that only safe and effective medicines are available in the market.
 
• It prevents the circulation of **substandard or counterfeit drugs**, safeguarding public health.
 
• India, as a major global supplier of generic medicines, requires **strong drug regulatory frameworks** to maintain its position in the global pharmaceutical industry.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Other Regulatory Initiatives:**
 
 
• The **Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940**, regulates the import, manufacture, distribution, and sale of drugs in India.
 
• The establishment of **Central Drugs Standard Control Organization (CDSCO)** ensures compliance with drug standards across India.
 
• Recent digital initiatives like **eSanjeevani** and the **National Digital Health Blueprint** aim to integrate technology into healthcare systems.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Ministry of Science and Technology:**

 
 
• Primarily focuses on scientific research, innovation, and technology development.
 
• It does not oversee drug regulation or healthcare initiatives.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers:**
 
 
• Responsible for the production and development of fertilizers, chemicals, and petrochemicals.
 
• The **Department of Pharmaceuticals** under this ministry focuses on pharmaceutical production but not regulatory frameworks.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Ayush:**
 
 
• Oversees the development of traditional medicine systems like Ayurveda, Yoga, Unani, Siddha, and Homeopathy.
 
• While it plays a role in promoting alternative medicine, it does not handle state drug regulatory systems.

questions.question: 22 March 2025 marks which important regional day in Bihar?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bihar Statehood Day**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bihar Statehood Day** is celebrated annually on **22 March** to commemorate the formation of Bihar as a separate state.
 
• This day marks the **historical event** in **1912**, when Bihar was carved out from the Bengal Presidency during British rule in India.
 
• The statehood of Bihar was part of the **British administrative reforms** aimed at improving governance by dividing the vast Bengal Presidency.
 
• Bihar was formed as an independent province, along with Orissa, under the **Government of India Act 1912**.
 
• The day is celebrated with **cultural events, public gatherings, and official ceremonies** across the state to honor its rich heritage and culture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Historical Context:**

 
 
• The **Bengal Presidency** was one of the largest administrative divisions during British rule, encompassing modern-day West Bengal, Bihar, Odisha, and parts of Assam.
 
• The **Government of India Act 1912** led to the division of Bengal into smaller provinces for better administrative efficiency.
 
• Bihar's separation was primarily driven by the need to address the unique cultural, linguistic, and administrative requirements of the region.
 
 
 
• **Geographical and Cultural Significance of Bihar:**
 
 
• Bihar is known for its rich **cultural heritage**, including ancient sites like **Nalanda University** and **Bodh Gaya**, which are of global importance.
 
• The state played a pivotal role in India's ancient history, being the center of major empires like **Magadha** and the birthplace of prominent religions like **Buddhism** and **Jainism**.
 
 
 
• **Celebrations and Observances:**
 
 
• Bihar Statehood Day is celebrated with **cultural programs, historical exhibitions, and government-led initiatives** to promote the state's heritage.
 
• Programs often include performances highlighting Bihar's **folk traditions, music, and dance forms**.
 
 
 
• **Economic and Political Importance:**
 
 
• Bihar is an important agricultural state, contributing significantly to India's **rice, wheat, and sugarcane** production.
 
• It is also a hub for industries like **handloom weaving, leather production, and tourism**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Formation of Bihar:**

 
 
• The separation of Bihar from Bengal was announced on **22 March 1912**, marking its establishment as a separate administrative province.
 
• This event was part of broader reforms by the British to decentralize governance and improve administrative efficiency in India.
 
 
 
• **Recognition of Heritage:**
 
 
• Bihar Statehood Day serves as an opportunity to reflect on the state's **historical contributions** and its role in shaping India's cultural and political landscape.
 
• The day is also used to promote awareness about Bihar's **tourism potential**, including its ancient heritage sites.

questions.question: Which lake, known as India’s longest and a Ramsar site in Kerala is currently facing severe ecological degradation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vembanad Lake**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vembanad Lake** is the **longest lake in India** and the **largest lake in Kerala**, stretching across multiple districts like Alappuzha, Kottayam, and Ernakulam.
 
• It has been designated as a **Ramsar site**, making it an internationally recognized wetland of ecological importance.
 
• The lake plays a critical role in Kerala's ecosystem, supporting a variety of **flora and fauna**, including migratory birds and aquatic species.
 
• It is a hub for activities like **fishing, agriculture, backwater tourism, and transportation**, contributing significantly to the local economy.
 
• Currently, the lake is facing severe **ecological degradation** due to issues like pollution, industrial waste, and encroachments, threatening its biodiversity and sustainability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Vembanad Lake – Features and Importance:**

 
 
• It spans an area of approximately **230 square kilometers** and is connected to multiple rivers like **Pamba, Meenachil, Achankovil, and Periyar**.
 
• The lake hosts the famous **Nehru Trophy Boat Race**, an annual event that draws tourists worldwide.
 
• It serves as a source of livelihood for thousands of local communities who rely on **fishing and agriculture**.
 
• The lake also supports unique ecosystems such as the **Kumarakom Bird Sanctuary**, a haven for migratory birds.
 
 
 
• **Other Options:**
 
 
• **Pulicat Lake:**
 
 
• Located between Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu, Pulicat is the **second-largest brackish water lake** in India.
 
• It is known for the **Pulicat Bird Sanctuary** and supports flamingos and other migratory birds.
 
• This lake does not face degradation at the same level as Vembanad Lake.
 
 
 
• **Chilika Lake:**
 
 
• Situated in Odisha, Chilika Lake is the **largest coastal lagoon** in India.
 
• It is also a Ramsar site and renowned for its **Irrawaddy dolphins** and migratory birds.
 
• Although Chilika Lake faces ecological concerns, the question specifically pertains to Kerala.
 
 
 
• **Loktak Lake:**
 
 
• Located in Manipur, Loktak Lake is famous for its floating islands called **phumdis**.
 
• It houses the **Keibul Lamjao National Park**, the world's only floating national park.
 
• While it is ecologically significant, it is not in Kerala.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Ecological Challenges at Vembanad Lake:**
 
 
• Increased levels of **pollution** due to industrial waste, urban runoff, and agricultural effluents.
 
• Encroachment and reclamation activities have led to the shrinkage of the lake area.
 
• Overfishing and unsustainable tourism have disrupted the lake's delicate **ecosystem balance**.
 
• The lack of effective management and conservation policies further exacerbates the degradation.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Ramsar Sites in Kerala:**

 
 
• Kerala is home to three Ramsar sites: **Vembanad Lake, Ashtamudi Lake**, and **Sasthamkotta Lake**.
 
• These wetlands are crucial for biodiversity conservation and act as natural buffers against flooding and other environmental challenges.
 
 
 
• **Conservation Efforts:**
 
 
• Various NGOs and state government initiatives are working toward restoring Vembanad Lake's ecosystem.
 
• Programs to reduce pollution, regulate fishing, and promote sustainable tourism are being implemented.
 
• Community participation is essential for effective conservation of the lake.

questions.question: In 2025, which of the following states emerged as the national leader in mangrove afforestation, covering 19020 hectares in just two years under the Centre’s ‘MISHTI’ scheme, launched in 2023?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gujarat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Under the Centre’s **Mangrove Initiative for Shoreline Habitats & Tangible Incomes (MISHTI)** scheme, **Gujarat** emerged as the national leader in mangrove afforestation, covering **19,020 hectares** between 2023 and 2025.
 
• The **MISHTI scheme**, launched in **2023**, aims to promote sustainable mangrove development and conservation in coastal regions across India.
 
• **Gujarat**, with its extensive coastline and favorable geographical conditions, played a pivotal role in achieving this milestone, contributing significantly to the scheme’s success.
 
• The initiative supports the restoration of degraded mangrove ecosystems, which are crucial for **carbon sequestration, biodiversity conservation, and coastal protection**.
 
• The state government collaborated with the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change** and local communities to successfully implement large-scale afforestation projects under MISHTI.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **MISHTI Scheme:**

 
 
• The **MISHTI scheme** was announced in the **Union Budget 2023-24** to facilitate the regeneration and conservation of mangroves in coastal states and union territories.
